retention_rule: Circuit Court of Cook County judges run unopposed in retention elections and need at least 60% 'Yes' votes to keep their seat. Circuit terms are 6 years and appellate terms 10 years (Injustice Watch). 60 circuit judges and 1 appellate justice are on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot.

notes: Newspaper recommendations: no Chicago Tribune or Chicago Sun-Times 2026 judicial retention endorsements were found (the search tool cannot reach chicagotribune.com), so 'newspapers' is null for every judge.
CBA rated all 60 retention judges 'Qualified' and published no per-judge narrative for retention.
The Alliance PDF gives each member bar's Yes/No; there is no single consensus rating. 'alliance' summarizes the 13 member votes. The ISBA and CCL are Alliance members and are also listed separately.

Flag rule used: 'concern' means a negative CBA, CCL or ISBA rating, or an Injustice Watch 'Notable controversy' flag. Antonietti and Molina-Gonzalez are marked 'clean' even though the Cook County Bar Association (an Alliance identity bar, not a major group under the rule) voted No. Their 'why' says so, and the caller may wish to reclassify them.

Spellings: CBA, CCL and the Alliance spell 'Maire Aileen Dempsey'; IW says she also uses 'Maire'. CCL and ISBA write 'Christ Stacey'; the CCL PDF misspells Antonietti as 'Antoinetti' and Tiesha Smith as 'Taisha'.

retention.assignment: First Municipal District, Civil Jury Section
retention.bio: Former Cook County assistant state's attorney (from 2003) and associate at Tristan & Cervantes. Brother of lobbyist Homero Tristan.

ratings.cba: Qualified (CBA Judicial Evaluation Committee, Sept. 24, 2026; all 60 retention judges found Qualified, no narrative given)

retention.assignment: Juvenile Justice Division (delinquency and juvenile expungements; a DCFS-involved calendar), since 2024
retention.bio: Former Cook County assistant public defender (2010–2020). She skipped bar evaluations in 2018 and 2020 and was rated Not Qualified then.

ratings.cba: Qualified (CBA Judicial Evaluation Committee, Sept. 24, 2026; all 60 retention judges found Qualified, no narrative given)
ratings.ccl: Qualified — but only after 'seeking an agreement from her to attend a Stress Management course'. Since her 2024 transfer 'there have been a number of problems reported with both her temperament and attendance'; practitioners describe 'a hostile temperament.'
ratings.isba: NOT RECOMMENDED (No) — 'Reports of screaming matches between the Judge and attorneys, and between the Judge and minor respondents cause concern about her temperament and effectiveness of her judicial performance.'

retention.injustice_watch: IW flag 'Negative ratings'. ISBA and five other bars (six per the Alliance PDF) said she should not be retained. She won in 2020 over the party-slated appointed judge without bar evaluation. She told IW she skipped 2018 for lack of experience and 2020 because the old ratings were still valid.
retention.why: ISBA 'Not Recommended' over 'screaming matches' with attorneys and minors, plus six more Alliance bars voting No. CCL said Qualified only after she agreed to a stress-management course amid reports of a 'hostile temperament' and attendance problems.
